Under a business-as-usual (BAU) scenario, China’s building life-cycle emissions are projected to peak in 2031–2033, while carbon neutrality remains challenged by persistent pressures from both material use and building operations. These pressures arise from the existing stock, whose continued use sustains energy demand while increasing building retirements shift construction from stock growth to the replacement of retired buildings. Implementing a high-efficiency scenario with regionally differentiated deployment of material- and energy-efficiency strategies could reduce China’s building-sector life-cycle emissions by 90% in 2060 relative to the BAU scenario. Provincial analysis further reveals that similar overall mitigation potential masks substantial differences in the composition of effective mitigation portfolios, reflecting local building-stock and energy-use characteristics. To close the remaining gap, deeper operational decarbonization should be coupled with stock-management strategies that extend building lifetimes, avoid premature demolition, and prioritize renovation and reuse.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c05362.title: Genetic Background and Metabolic Influence on Long-Term Lithium Bioaccumulation in Mytilus Mussels and Their Hybrids
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c05362.summary: Abstract Marine mussels are widely used as sentinel organisms in coastal biomonitoring, yet the biological mechanisms controlling the bioaccumulation of emerging metals remain poorly constrained. Climate change and anthropogenic disturbances are reshaping species distributions and contact zones, promoting mussel hybridization that may alter physiological traits and contaminant-handling capacities. Lithium (Li) remains largely overlooked despite its potential toxicity and rapidly increasing global demand. Here, we investigate the influence of critical factors on Li bioaccumulation by mussels combining genetic background and isotopic approaches. Progenies of two Mytilus species and their hybrids were transplanted to the same Atlantic coastal site for 12 months. Over this in situ exposure period, Li concentrations show comparable temporal trends across all progeny groups, with an initial uptake-dominated phase followed by biodilution. Lithium isotope ratios (δ7Li) display a coherent temporal trend across all groups (decrease at early exposure, increase during later growth), and the magnitude of the shift differs slightly among genetic backgrounds. Across samples, δ7Li is coupled to growth-related metrics (dry weight) and inversely related to Li concentrations, indicating a metabolic control on Li isotope compositions of these organisms. Li concentrations are also positively correlated with lithogenic-associated elements (e.g., aluminum), consistent with the influence of particle associated Li. A simplified biodynamic modeling including Li isotopes data further indicates a more efficient Li depuration after 5 months, combined with a relatively stronger contribution from dissolved Li. Overall, growth-related factors emerged as the primary biological drivers of Li concentration and isotope variability, with the relative contributions of dissolved and particulate exposure pathways varying in association with physiological growth. Hybridization may modulate Li bioaccumulation and δ7Li values, but its influence appears secondary and does not compromise the use of Mytilus mussels as bioindicators in established frameworks such as “Mussel Watch”.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c11284.title: Can the Spatial Planning of Livestock Production Tackle Future Nitrogen Pollution in China?
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c11284.summary: Abstract Nitrogen (N) pollution from livestock production significantly threatens China’s air and water quality, necessitating innovative solutions to balance food security and environmental sustainability. Studies have mostly overlooked the spatial heterogeneity of N-related environmental impacts and the trade-offs between reducing ammonia (NH3) emissions and N concentrations in water. This study develops a spatially explicit multiscale model system encompassing 13,000 polygons across China to assess soil N balance, NH3 emission intensity, and N concentrations in surface water, aiming to explore integrated spatial-planning (SP) strategies that maximize synergy and minimize trade-offs. Our findings reveal that single-purpose SP scenarios (e.g., reducing NH3 emissions or instream N concentrations) can effectively address one N-related issue but produce substantial trade-offs, leaving >50% of China’s population exposed to at least another N-related problem. However, an integrated SP approach could reduce harmful N exposures for 90% of China’s population while ensuring food security. This approach involves reallocating 14% of livestock production, reducing livestock numbers by one-third relative to the 2050 baseline, and implementing advanced technologies to mitigate N pollution hotspots. Thus, our findings emphasize the importance of spatially explicit N boundaries and multicriteria planning to tackle N pollution in air and water simultaneously, supporting cross-media N management policy-making and region-specific strategies.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c16475.title: Embedding Environmental Science and Technology into Sustainability

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c07560.title: Energy Supply and Demand Coordination Can Advance Both Climate Goals and Sustainable Development in the Global South
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c07560.summary: Abstract Reconciling climate mitigation with sustainable development is a critical imperative in the Global South, where rising emissions coincide with persistent development deficits. Here, we develop an integrated assessment framework linking nationally determined contribution (NDC)-aligned supply-side, demand-side, and coordinated supply–demand policy packages to greenhouse-gas trajectories and a six-goal Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) scorecard. We show that supply-focused renewable expansion or demand-focused efficiency improves selected SDG-related dimensions but creates trade-offs involving energy-cost pressure, water use, and ecosystem protection. By comparison, an integrated supply–demand strategy maximizes the SDG score (69 versus 65 under REF in 2050), enhances clean-energy penetration and efficiency, and averts approximately 485,000 annual premature deaths in 2050 relative to REF. These findings highlight the potential of coordinated supply–demand strategies to reduce climate–SDG trade-offs across the Global South.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c14070.title: ES&T Next 60 Years: Sustainability and Climate Change

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c10597.title: Spatiotemporal Orchestration of Dual Functional Sites Enables Efficacious NH3-SCR and CO Oxidation: Synergy of Zeolite-Associated Cu Sites and Cu-O-Co Interfacial Ensembles
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c10597.summary: Abstract Integrated abatement of NOx and CO is highly desirable for industrial flue-gas purification, yet competitive adsorption and mismatched kinetic requirements between NH3–SCR and CO oxidation hinder the realization of a unified low-temperature reaction window. Herein, a spatiotemporally organized Cu–O–Co/Cu-ZSM-5 architecture was constructed to provide differentiated catalytic environments and reduce mutual interference between the two reactions. The optimized Co0.2@Cu/Cu-Z5 catalyst delivers a broad co-operational window of 150–350 °C at 45,000 mL·h–1·g–1 and sustains simultaneous NO and CO conversions above 80% from 175 to 350 °C even at 175,000 mL·h–1·g–1, with high N2 selectivity and robust tolerance to 5 vol % H2O. In situ DRIFTS and transient cross-interference experiments indicate that zeolite-associated Cu species preferentially sustain NH3–SCR functionality, whereas Cu–O–Co interfacial ensembles preferentially enhance CO/NO oxidation, thereby alleviating mutual inhibition under coupled conditions. Theoretical calculations further reveal interfacial electron redistribution, Cu 3d-Co 3d hybridization, and more favorable oxygen-vacancy formation at the CuO/Co3O4 interface, and the CuO/Co3O4 interface lowers the activation barrier of the carbonate-forming elementary step from 2.12 to 0.36 eV via a carbonate-assisted MVK-like pathway, whereas its low activation barrier for the first NH3 dehydrogenation step (0.41 eV) suggests the necessity of confining NH3 activation to Cu-zeolite sites to avoid parasitic oxidation. This dual-center pathway differentiation alleviates adsorption and kinetic conflicts between competing reactions, offering a strategy for improving compatibility in multifunctional environmental catalysis.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c10583.title: Temperature Does Not Universally Accelerate VOC–OH Reaction Kinetics: Implications for Ozone Formation

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c12655.title: Endocrine-Disrupting Effects and Reproductive Toxicity of Metal-Based Nanoparticles through DRP1-Mediated Mitophagy within an Adverse Outcome Pathway Framework
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c12655.summary: Abstract The widespread use of metal-based nanoparticles (NPs), including Ag, ZnO, and TiO2 NPs, in industrial and consumer products has raised concerns about their potential endocrine-disrupting effects and reproductive toxicity. Conventional safety assessment approaches may not adequately capture the complex mechanisms underlying NP-induced toxicity. To our knowledge, this study is the first to integrate OECD-recommended assays, high-throughput screening, an adverse outcome pathway (AOP) framework, and the Toxicological Prioritization Index (ToxPi) to investigate the endocrine-disrupting effects and reproductive toxicity of metal-based NPs. The results showed that ZnO and Ag NPs increased estrogen receptor (ER) transcriptional activity, whereas TiO2 NPs inhibited it. All NPs increased 17β-estradiol production, while ZnO and TiO2 NPs reduced testosterone production. ZnO NPs induced the generation of reactive oxygen species, mitochondrial dysfunction, and DRP1 activation, which were associated with subsequent apoptosis, mitophagy, and autophagy. In contrast, Ag NPs did not induce apoptosis or autophagy, suggesting distinct cytotoxic mechanisms. TiO2 NPs caused no significant cell death in MLTC-1 cells, even at high concentrations. ToxPi ranked COOH-ZnO NPs as the most toxic, followed by NH2–ZnO NPs, Ag NPs, and TiO2 NPs. This integrated framework could provide a practical approach for toxicity screening, mechanistic investigation, and hazard prioritization of NPs.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c09027.title: Origins, Current Practice, and Future Directions of Life Cycle Assessment
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c09027.summary: Abstract Life cycle assessment (LCA) has evolved from a niche method for evaluating product systems into a widely used approach for assessing the environmental sustainability of products, services, supply chains, technologies, sectors, economies, and scenarios. This article reflects on its historical roots, current state, and future developments. The early development was marked by pioneering methodological frameworks, inventory databases, and impact-assessment methods. Since then, LCA has matured into a robust and versatile method. Today, scientific, industry-related, and regional inventory databases support routine assessments, while impact assessment has increased in scope, accuracy, regional representation, and policy relevance. Advances in inventory modeling, impact assessment, regionalization, uncertainty analysis, and prospective assessment have substantially broadened the questions that LCA can address and the decision contexts it can support. While LCA traditionally focused on comparative assessments, recent advances introduced absolute approaches that benchmark impacts against planetary-boundary-based thresholds. Looking forward, artificial intelligence promises to transform LCA by facilitating data collection, enabling large-scale scenario analysis, and accelerating assessments. Moreover, increasing spatial and temporal resolution will be a game-changer for assessing impacts such as biodiversity loss and climate change.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c09731.title: Magnetic Properties of Heated Fe-Rich Soils as Proxies for Burn Temperature and Nanoparticulate Formation
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c09731.summary: Abstract Wildfires are increasing in frequency and severity worldwide, exposing large populations to iron-oxide aerosols and metal-bearing particulates generated during soil burning. Yet the formation and thermochemical alteration of iron oxides during fire, and their implications for exposure and risk assessment, remain poorly constrained. Here, we investigate how iron-oxide populations evolve with temperature using heating-based experiments on Fe-rich serpentinite and greenstone soils. A comprehensive suite of magnetic measurements reveals systematic shifts toward more oxidized phases and finer particle sizes with increasing temperature. Different magnetic measurements resolve complementary aspects of temperature-driven iron-oxide transformations: hysteresis properties most clearly track changes in the single-phase-dominated serpentinite soils, whereas remanent coercivity distributions effectively resolve the evolution of multiple coexisting magnetic phases in the greenstone soils. Across both lithologies, the relative contribution of magnetite and its associated low-temperature Verwey transition diminishes with increasing oxidation, while ultrafine (<∼30 nm) magnetic particles and hematite become increasingly abundant, particularly under the highest heating conditions (600–800 °C). More broadly, our findings highlight the potential for rock magnetic methods to aid in reconstructing past burn intensities and quantifying fire-induced nanoparticulate formation, with the latter providing information relevant to assessing potential public health risks in fire-prone regions.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c07913.title: Robust Dual-Cycle Direct Air Capture Process Enabled by a Novel Biphasic Solvent
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c07913.summary: Abstract Traditional liquid-based DAC (L-DAC) technology suffers from high energy consumption and transportation difficulties due to complex intermediate conversion and oxidative degradation, despite its fast kinetics. To address these challenges, this study proposed a dual-cycle DAC strategy using a novel biphasic absorbent ([PZ][1,2,4]-NMP). Atmospheric CO2 was first captured by KOH and converted to K2CO3. Subsequently, under air-isolated conditions, [PZ][1,2,4] selectively displaced CO2 from K2CO3, concentrating it into a flowable carbamate slurry. By confining regeneration to this small-volume slurry, a low-energy penalty of 1.37–1.45 GJ·t–1CO2 was achieved. The closed-loop design effectively prevented oxidative degradation of the active components and significantly enhanced phase separation. This dual-cycle architecture provides a promising pathway for energy-efficient and operationally robust DAC technologies.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c09462.title: Distinct Methane-Cycling Pathways Drive Variable Surface Flux in Freshwater Wetlands
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c09462.summary: Abstract Freshwater wetlands are the largest natural source of methane (CH4), representing a third of global emissions. Both CH4 production and oxidation are microbially mediated, yet the metabolic controls governing CH4 cycling across wetland types remain poorly resolved. Here, we investigated six hydrologically and geochemically distinct wetlands in the Prairie Pothole Region of North America. By integrating genome-resolved metatranscriptomic data with porewater geochemistry, dissolved CH4 profiles, and chamber-based flux measurements across these wetlands, we assessed how microbial gene expression associated with electron acceptor utilization corresponds to CH4 cycling and identified the dominant methanogenic pathways driving CH4 production. CH4 porewater concentration varied across seasons and sites, with higher concentrations later in the season under more reducing conditions. Wetlands with higher expression of denitrification and sulfate reduction genes exhibited lower methanogenesis and porewater CH4 concentrations. Sites with higher porewater CH4 showed elevated expression of all three methanogenic pathways. Methanogenic activity, however, was not predictive of surface flux. Instead, emissions were modulated by site-specific physical and geochemical controls on methanotrophic CH4 consumption. These findings demonstrate that equivalent CH4 production can emerge through distinct microbial pathways, and that production alone is a poor predictor of atmospheric emissions. This distinction carries important implications for modeling wetland contributions to global CH4 budgets.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c08418.title: Developing Partial Characterization Factors for Ship Noise Impacts on Marine Biodiversity in European Seas
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c08418.summary: Abstract Shipping is the primary source of underwater noise pollution, yet its impacts on marine biodiversity remain unquantified in Life Cycle Impact Assessment (LCIA). This study presents the first framework for quantifying the regionalized impact of ship noise on marine mammal biodiversity within LCIA, demonstrated for European Seas. Ship noise data from the NAVISON project for 2019 were combined with species-specific sensitivity thresholds for marine mammals to derive spatially explicit Potentially Affected Fractions (PAF). Partial characterization factors (pCFs) for 21 country groups were calculated by integrating PAF values with spatially explicit transport work and maritime trade data, ranging from zero to 1.00 × 10–14 PAF × yr × ton-km–1 (Northern Europe), with a mean of 1.86 × 10–15 PAF × yr × ton-km–1. The total impact of ship noise per country was calculated for 200 countries by multiplying the pCF with each country’s maritime trade. The United Kingdom has the highest total impact (1.34× 10–2 PAF × yr), followed by the United States of America and Spain. This framework represents a first step toward integrating ship noise as a novel impact category in LCIA, supporting comprehensive environmental assessments of global supply chains alongside other maritime stressors such as greenhouse gas emissions and marine invasive species.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c10708.title: Cross-Domain Tracing of Rice Stem Stress under Soil Cadmium Pollution
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c10708.summary: Abstract Plants exposed to heavy-metal-contaminated soil are subjected to pollutant pressure, making timely monitoring of plant condition important for assessing their responses to soil pollution. Although spectral sensing is widely used for nondestructive monitoring of plant stress, the cross-domain association between plant optical signals and Cd-induced physiological responses remains unclear. Here, we integrated spectral sensing with deep learning, Monte Carlo simulation, and omics analysis to systematically explore how spectral signals and physiological responses jointly support the monitoring of Cd-induced stress in rice stems. We found that Cd exposure reorganized interface-associated stress, protective chemistry, and redox regulation into coordinated Defense, Repair, and Adjustment signatures. These biological changes were differentially expressed across the visible, red-edge, and near-infrared spectral regions, producing a reweighting of absorption- and scattering-sensitive information. The agreement between spectral variation and biological stress signatures further established a cross-domain link between stress-state formation and optical detection. Benefiting from this mechanism, we achieved high-accuracy nondestructive detection of rice stem Cd content and noninvasive characterization of Cd-induced responses. A portable spectrometer–smartphone implementation further demonstrated field-oriented feasibility. These findings provide a biological and optical basis for tracking stress progression and supporting timely, feedback-guided crop management.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c08598.title: Screening Environmental Toxicants for Neurodevelopmental Disorders Using a hPSC-Based Mitochondrial Redox Biosensor
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c08598.summary: Abstract Environmental chemical exposure during prenatal development significantly elevates the risk of neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs), with mitochondrial oxidative stress representing a central convergent mechanism. However, existing screening platforms lack the genetic stability and developmental stage specificity required for systematic identification of neurotoxic hazards across human neural lineage progression. Here, we established a human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC)-based mitochondrial redox biosensor by CRISPR/Cas9-mediated targeted integration of the genetically encoded H2O2 probe mito-HyPer7 into the AAVS1 safe-harbor locus, ensuring stable expression across pluripotent, neurogenic, and neuronal stages. Using this platform, we screened 76 epidemiologically relevant industrial chemicals and identified reactive oxygen species-inducing toxicants (ROS-ITs) with lineage-stage-selective profiles across neural lineages. Neural progenitor cells (NPCs) exhibited the broadest sensitivity spectrum, revealing neurogenesis as a critical developmental window. Among the screened compounds, bisphenol G (BPG)─an emerging alternative in plastic production─displayed cross-stage toxicity surpassing that of bisphenol A (BPA). In three-dimensional cortical organoids, BPG impaired radial glial cell (RGC) proliferation, triggered precocious neurogenic transition, and induced apoptosis, culminating in disrupted cortical architecture. Mechanistically, BPG aberrantly activated thyroid hormone receptor (TR)-mediated transcription, and the resulting developmental impairment was partially ameliorated by the receptor antagonist NH-3. Collectively, this study presents an integrative framework that unites a genetically stable platform for high-throughput mitochondrial redox screening with organoid-based pathological and mechanistic validation, providing a comprehensive paradigm for identifying and characterizing environmental toxicants that threaten human neurodevelopment.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c10311.title: Broad Nuclear Receptor-Binding Activities of Phase II Sulfate Metabolites Revealed by the Combinatorial Synthesis for Environmental Research (CoSyER) Approach with Affinity Selection Mass Spectrometry (ASMS)
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c10311.summary: Abstract Biotransformation alters the bioactivity of xenobiotics in humans; however, traditional approaches are infeasible for testing large numbers of metabolites. Herein, we propose a high-throughput combinatorial synthesis for environmental research and a protein affinity selection mass spectrometry approach (CoSyER:ASMS) for assessing the receptor-binding activities of hundreds of metabolites within weeks. As proof of concept, 132 sulfate metabolites were synthesized from 222 ToxCast chemicals using an optimized one-pot combinatorial synthesis approach. Four nuclear receptors (PPARγ, PXR, ERRγ, and FXR) were further selected for AS-MS analysis to evaluate the binding activities of 132 sulfate metabolites and corresponding parent compounds, covering 1056 binary interactions. Interestingly, sulfate metabolites exhibited broad nuclear receptor-binding activities toward PPARγ and PXR, with 29 and 24 ligands detected by AS-MS, respectively. Bioactivities and functional effects of triclosan sulfate and 1-hydroxypyrene sulfate were validated by orthogonal fluorescence assay and human cell receptor assays. Collectively, this study introduces CoSyER:ASMS as a scalable platform integrating high-throughput generation of sulfate metabolites with receptor-binding screening to accelerate the toxicological prioritization of this understudied metabolite class.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c11597.title: Air–Water Interfacial Secondary Hydroxylation of SO2: An Overlooked and Rapid Pathway to Sulfuric Acid in Tropical Coastal Industrial Areas
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c11597.summary: Abstract Atmospheric sulfuric acid (H2SO4) is a key driver of acid deposition, aerosol growth, and new particle formation. Its formation is initiated by rapid OH addition to SO2 to produce HOSO2, but direct hydroxylation of HOSO2 is kinetically unfavorable. Consequently, the accepted route to H2SO4 proceeds via O2 oxidation of HOSO2 to SO3, followed by hydrolysis. Here, using classical molecular dynamics (MD) and Born–Oppenheimer MD simulations, we identify an alternative interfacial pathway that directly converts HOSO2 and OH into H2SO4. Strong interfacial affinity of both reactants drives this transformation at the air–water interface with a free-energy barrier of only 1.73 kcal·mol–1, substantially lower than that of gas-phase SO3 hydrolysis. Kinetic analysis further indicates that, under conditions of elevated OH, HOSO2, and low SO3, this pathway can outpace gas-phase SO3 hydrolysis by more than 3 orders of magnitude. These results reveal an efficient interfacial source of atmospheric H2SO4, offering a mechanistic basis for its elevated abundance in polluted coastal environments and improving the representation of sulfur oxidation in atmospheric models.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c09994.title: Internal Molecular Response Chains to Inhaled Volatile Organic Compounds for Precision Health Risk Assessment Revealed by Breathomics
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c09994.summary: Abstract Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are airborne pollutants, yet risk assessment based solely on external concentrations may miss internal molecular effects under low-level mixture exposure. We collected exhaled breath and ambient air samples from 67 child volunteers for VOC profiling, with blood samples from 16 participants used for transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses. A physiological compartment-based kinetic model identified 76 endogenous and 44 exogenous VOCs in breath, and dimensionality reduction grouped exogenous VOCs into seven chemically interpretable exposure patterns. These patterns were associated with 86 genes involving cell cycle and neural pathways and nominally with 247 metabolites, suggesting potential variation in energy, lipid and amino acid metabolism, and neurotransmitter homeostasis. Multiomics integration further suggested seven endogenous VOCs as candidate signals reflecting variation across exposure, transcriptome, and metabolome layers. Benzothiazole, 3,7-dimethyl-nonane, and 2-methyl-2-propenoic acid were associated with both conventional cancer risk estimates and cancer pathway activity, whereas conventional cancer risk showed only weak correlation with this internal phenotype. These findings support an internal molecular response framework connecting inhaled VOC exposure to biological effects and highlight the potential of breathomics for precision health risk assessment.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c11702.title: Dust Storms as Dynamic Multipollutant Exposure Systems: Environmental Transformation, Toxicological Mechanisms, and Health Implications
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c11702.summary: Abstract Dust particles have long been considered to be naturally derived mineral particles. However, with the increase in regional anthropogenic emissions and atmospheric multipollutant processes, their environmental significance as pollutant carriers and multicomponent exposure media has increasingly attracted attention. Nevertheless, existing studies have primarily focused on dust event characteristics, variations in particulate matter concentrations, or the effects of individual pollutant components, while a systematic understanding of the formation processes and health implications of dust as a dynamic multipollutant exposure system remains limited. This review conceptualizes dust storms as a dynamic multipollutant exposure system and integrates evidence from environmental chemistry, exposure science, toxicology, and epidemiology to discuss the environmental behavior of dust-associated pollutant components, their potential mechanisms of action, and their associations with population health effects. This review aims to advance the understanding of the processes underlying health risks associated with dust storms and provide a scientific basis for the development of future dust-related health risk assessment frameworks.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c10276.title: Forensic Accounting of Kelp Carbon Sequestration: Geomorphic and Microbial Controls on Permanence and Verifiability
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c10276.summary: Abstract Kelp forests fix substantial amounts of carbon, but the fraction reaching long-term storage remains unclear. This review uses forensic accounting to assess evidence for kelp carbon sequestration, focusing on geomorphic and microbial controls on permanence and verifiability. Studies show kelp production and export, while retention estimates depend on the receiving environment and assessment period. Kelp-derived particulate carbon has been detected in deep water and sediments, whereas the long-term fate of kelp-derived dissolved organic carbon (DOC) remains poorly quantified. Geomorphology affects transport distance, source–sink connectivity, and access to depositional environments. Microbial processing controls degradation and remineralization and can generate recalcitrant DOC through the microbial carbon pump (MCP). Short transport pathways and slower degradation can increase particulate delivery, but retention also depends on circulation, ventilation, and postdepositional loss. For carbon remineralized to dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC), storage duration depends on remineralization depth and water-mass ventilation. Persistent DOC storage estimates require source attribution, pool size, and residence time. We link each carbon claim to measurements in the receiving reservoir and distinguish marine carbon storage from net atmospheric CO2 removal and project-level crediting. Integrating source attribution, transport, microbial transformation, and reservoir retention can improve storage estimates and guide monitoring.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c02499.title: Mind the Leak: Challenges of Riverbank Filtration for Highly Mobile Chemical Pollutants
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c02499.summary: Abstract Riverbank filtration (RBF) serves as a natural protective barrier for groundwater and drinking water sources. Growing evidence indicates that RBF is minimally effective at removing persistent, mobile, and toxic (PMT) substances, as well as very persistent and very mobile (vPvM) substances, which have recently been established as new hazard classes in the European Union. Owing to their resistance to biodegradation and sorption, these chemicals, including many pesticides, pharmaceuticals, and industrial chemicals, can bypass wastewater treatment and natural riverbank barriers, ultimately contaminating groundwater and abstraction wells for drinking water. Current data gaps as well as analytical challenges hinder identification of PMT/vPvM substances in riverbank filtrate. One major data gap is that many of these substances are transformation products, some of which are formed by riverbank transformation processes. Varying geochemical and transient flow conditions further complicate prediction of the transport and fate of PMT substances, and the evolution of water quality, within RBF systems. To address these challenges, this Perspective proposes a progressive management strategy that integrates source reduction, reactive transport simulations, and nontargeted monitoring, as well as advanced multibarrier treatment, aimed at preventing and mitigating risks from PMT/vPvM substances in RBF systems.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c10664.title: Toxicity-Weighted Assessment Reveals the Rising Dominance of Non-Exhaust PM2.5 from On-Road Transportation in China
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c10664.summary: Abstract Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) emitted from nonexhaust sources, here defined as brake and tire wear, is attracting attention as vehicle exhaust emissions decline due to advanced aftertreatment devices and rapid fleet electrification. However, the relative toxicity of nonexhaust PM2.5 compared with tailpipe emissions remains insufficiently quantified under a unified methodology. In this study, oxidative stress and cytotoxicity potencies of nonexhaust PM2.5 are 5- to 11-fold higher than those of exhaust PM2.5 via dynamometer tests, chemical analyses, and in vitro cellular assays. By integrating these toxic potencies with compiled emission inventories and modeling, toxicity-adjusted emissions of nonexhaust PM2.5 in 2023 expanded to nearly eight times those of exhaust PM2.5 in China. Exposure hotspots were disproportionately concentrated in economically developed regions with dense traffic. Projections forecast the nonexhaust proportion in toxicity-adjusted on-road emissions to surge from 54% in 2014 to an overwhelming 96% by 2050. While fleet electrification eliminates tailpipe exhaust and regenerative braking reduces brake wear, the nonexhaust PM2.5 proportion will keep rising in the absence of dedicated control measures. Our findings underscore an urgent imperative to incorporate nonexhaust sources into future air quality management, prioritizing eco-friendly material innovations and establishing standardized regulatory metrics to safeguard public health.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c13060.title: Physiological and Transcriptomic Responses of Thalassiosira pseudonana to Coated ZnO Nanoparticles and Their Mixtures under Long-Term, Low-Dose Exposure: The Dominant Role of Dissolved Zinc
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c13060.summary: Abstract The escalating production of engineered nanomaterials has raised concerns about their environmental impact. However, conventional short-term, high-dose ecotoxicity studies inadequately reflect realistic exposure scenarios. This study evaluated the long-term, low-dose toxicity of bare zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnO-NPs) and four representative silane-modified ZnO-NPs in the marine diatom Thalassiosira pseudonana. Algal cells were exposed for 14 days to individual ZnO-NPs, their binary mixtures (0.001–1 mg/L) or equimolar Zn2+ (0.0008–0.8 mg/L). Physiological and transcriptomic responses showed dose- and time-dependent toxicity, with largely comparable effects across nanoparticle and Zn2+ treatments. Growth inhibition by all zinc forms peaked at 38.0% within 0.01–0.1 mg/L and exceeded 90.0% at 1 mg/L, accompanied by reduced photosynthetic performance, altered chlorophyll a content, and elevated lipid peroxidation. Transcriptomic profiles of all ZnO-NPs resembled those of Zn2+, particularly for photosynthesis- and oxidative stress-related pathways. These similar responses were likely attributable to the substantial dissolution of all nanoparticles and their mixtures (44.3–89.2%), resulting in comparable cellular zinc bioaccumulation and Zn2+-like toxicity. Together, these findings reflect that the tested ZnO-NPs, whether silane-modified or present in mixtures, may behave similarly to dissolved zinc under chronic, environmentally relevant concentrations, highlighting the importance of incorporating such scenarios into ecological risk assessments of soluble metal-based nanomaterials.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c15978.title: Is Regional Conflict an Environmental Risk Multiplier for the Arabian Gulf and Gulf of Oman? Toxicological and Engineering Considerations

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c10303.title: Underappreciated Role of Free Troposphere–Boundary Layer Exchange in Ozone Pollution over the North China Plain
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c10303.summary: Abstract Ozone pollution control is mainly based on the ozone chemistry sensitivity to precursor emissions. However, despite stringent reductions in precursor emissions, severe summer ozone pollution persistently engulfs the North China Plain (NCP), urgently calling for effective ozone controls. Here, we show that there is strong interfacial ozone exchange between free troposphere (FT) and atmospheric boundary layer (ABL), which renders FT ozone a potential source of surface ozone, but has not been well accounted for in previous ozone controls. We quantify FT-ABL interfacial ozone exchange using an online diagnostic scheme implemented in a coupled meteorology-chemistry model and reveal a significant yet spatially heterogeneous correlation between observed surface ozone and interfacial exchange over the NCP. In high-correlation area, strong downward transport from FT to ABL exceeds chemical production, contributing 52% of afternoon ozone sources under polluted conditions. In low-correlation area, ozone pollution is dominated by chemical production. Derived from these spatially differentiated pollution causes, we propose an expanded ozone pollution formation regime to divide the NCP into exchange-dominated, chemistry-dominated, and mixed conditions. This new regime can better explain observed and modeled spatial differences of ozone trends in response to precursor reductions in 2019–2025. Our results highlight the importance of incorporating FT-ABL interfacial exchange into ozone pollution control frameworks beyond conventional chemistry-based regime.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c04344.title: Decoding and Harnessing Microbial Resilience for Anaerobic Digestion: Mechanisms, Strategies, and Sustainability under Environmental Stress
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c04344.summary: Abstract Anaerobic digestion (AD) is central to the circular bioeconomy, yet its application is limited by the vulnerability of microbial consortia to diverse stressors from endogenous metabolic inhibitors to exogenous contaminants. This Review synthesizes current evidence on microbial resilience mechanisms in AD, distinguishing resistance from perturbation to functional recovery through a sensing-activation-adaptation cascade. The thermodynamic basis of stability is examined through discoveries in direct interspecies electron transfer (DIET) and metabolic bifurcation, revealing how syntrophic networks overcome thermodynamic barriers under stress. Multiscale resilience mechanisms are considered from molecular sensors and signal transduction pathways to community-level reorganization associated with functional redundancy and niche differentiation. Bridging microbial ecology with process engineering, resilience-enhancing strategies are evaluated, including quorum sensing manipulation, conductive material amendment, and bioaugmentation with immobilized consortia, strengthening syntrophic networks under internal and external perturbations. A shift from reactive monitoring to proactive management is discussed, using interpretable deep learning models and genome-informed digital twins to predict failures. Critical knowledge gaps include single-cell phenotypic heterogeneity and the synthetic consortium design. Resilient AD systems require a framework integrating techno-economic viability with life cycle assessment, ensuring that they are biologically robust, environmentally sustainable, and economically competitive under variable operating conditions.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c08145.title: Physiological Adaptation of Comammox Nitrospira to Acidic pH Suppresses N2O Production
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c08145.summary: Abstract Nitrous oxide (N2O), a potent greenhouse gas, is a major byproduct of microbial nitrification, yet how environmental pH governs N2O production by complete ammonia oxidizers (comammox) remains poorly understood. We conducted controlled culture experiments with comammox Nitrospira inopinata at pH 6.5, 7.5, and 8.5. Under mild acidification (pH 6.5), nitrification activity was largely maintained, but cellular growth declined sharply, and both N2O yield and extracellular hydroxylamine (NH2OH) accumulation fell substantially relative to neutral conditions. Strikingly, this reduced growth was accompanied by pronounced transcriptional upregulation of core nitrification, stress response, and pH homeostasis genes, whereas carbon fixation genes remained largely unchanged. This decoupling of growth from gene expression indicates that acid-stressed cells reallocate energy away from biosynthesis toward cellular maintenance and proton extrusion, tightening intracellular handling of NH2OH and limiting its extracellular release. Isotopomer analysis (site preference ∼28–36‰) confirmed that NH2OH-driven chemistry remained the dominant N2O source across all pH conditions, and complementary abiotic assays indicated that chemical N2O formation was likely influenced by the diminished NH2OH pool. These results establish that comammox suppresses, rather than enhances, N2O production under mild acidification, opposite to the response reported for canonical ammonia-oxidizing microbes. This distinctive trait carries important implications for predicting nitrification-derived N2O fluxes and refining greenhouse-gas budgets in acidifying ecosystems.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c07646.title: Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) in Textiles: Attributing the Fluorine Inventory via Polymer-Specific Analysis
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c07646.summary: Abstract Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are widely used in functional textiles for water- and stain resistance, yet their polymer compositions, quantities, and potential environmental release remain poorly resolved by conventional analyses. Here, we analyzed 22 commercial textiles using an integrated approach combining total fluorine (TF) by combustion ion chromatography, targeted PFAS analysis, the total oxidizable precursor (TOP) assay, and pyrolysis–gas chromatography–high-resolution mass spectrometry (Py-GC-HRMS); the latter enabled polymer-specific identification and semiquantitative estimation of fluoropolymer and side-chain fluorinated polymer (SCFP) contributions. Fifteen textiles contained low-to-moderate TF concentrations (0.03–2.57 mg F g–1) and were predominantly associated with SCFPs containing 6:2 and/or 8:2 fluorotelomer moieties, whereas three high-fluorine textiles (143–158 mg F g–1) contained polytetrafluoroethylene together with SCFP-based treatments. Targeted PFAS accounted for ≤0.021% of TF, while TOP-derived PFAS also represented only a small additional fraction, indicating that conventional extractable and oxidizable PFAS measurements captured little of the total fluorine inventory. Simulated laundering, UV exposure, and wet abrasion caused limited TF loss in most textiles but substantial losses in some SCFP-treated materials, indicating treatment-dependent potential for PFAS-associated fluorine release during use and aging. This approach improves polymer-specific characterization of PFAS in textiles and helps assess their potential environmental emissions.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c10878.title: Mechanochemistry-Induced Hydrated Salt Activation for Green Recovery of Palladium and Platinum via O 2 -Mediated Oxidation
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c10878.summary: Abstract Palladium (Pd) and platinum (Pt) are essential precious metals in modern catalytic applications, while their sustainable recovery remains a significant challenge. Herein, we report a room-temperature, AlCl3·6H2O-assisted mechanochemical strategy for efficient recovery of Pd and Pt from industrial spent catalysts and automotive three-way catalysts without the addition of external oxidants. Mechanistic investigations reveal that mechanochemical treatment promotes catalyst fragmentation and the activation of hydrated salt, creating an ion-rich, liquid-like interfacial environment that facilitates O2-mediated oxidation of metallic Pd and Pt and stabilizes the oxidized metal species through chloride coordination. High-purity Pd and Pt products were successfully recovered through water extraction and N2H4·H2O reduction, while the recyclable AlCl3·6H2O medium enabled a closed-loop process with reduced reagent consumption. A preliminary lab-scale cost assessment indicated treatment costs comparable to those of conventional aqua regia treatment, highlighting the potential of hydrated salt-assisted mechanochemistry as a mild, recyclable, and economically promising approach for sustainable Pd and Pt recovery.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c11064.title: Quantifying the Vehicle Emission Reduction Required to Offset Warming-Driven Ozone Increase in Beijing
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c11064.summary: Abstract Vehicle emissions (VE) reductions are a key pathway for mitigating urban ozone pollution, but their effectiveness under the condition of warming-driven biogenic emission responses remains unclear. An ozone formation path tracing (OFPT) method coupling an observation-based model (OBM) with Positive Matrix Factorization (PMF) was used to quantify the contribution of different VOCs for different emission sources to the ozone production rate (PO3). In this study, initial VOC concentrations were reconstructed by correcting for photochemical losses, and an additional constraint on isoprene was applied to improve the assessment of ozone production in Beijing. The results show that initial VOC reconstruction substantially increased PO3 and changed source attribution. Biogenic emissions became the largest single contributor to PO3, whereas VE remained the dominant controllable anthropogenic source because it supplied both VOCs and NOx. After considering the temperature response of isoprene emissions, a 10.7 ± 3.5% reduction in VE was required to offset the O3 increase caused by a 1 °C temperature rise under current conditions. Future-scenario simulations showed that the required VE reductions were lower under the Clean Air scenario (7.1 ± 0.7%) than under the Baseline scenario (11.3 ± 0.1%). These results highlight the need to integrate vehicle electrification, biogenic VOC responses, and warming effects into future ozone control strategies.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c11325.title: An Innovative Ion Chromatography Method for Determination of Hydroxymethanesulfonate (HMS) in Ambient Air
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c11325.summary: Abstract Hydroxymethanesulfonate (HMS) is a substantial contributor to atmospheric particulate sulfur, yet its accurate quantification remains challenging due to chemical instability, poor chromatographic separation from sulfate, and the lack of a robust routine filter method. Here, we developed a hydrogen peroxide (H2O2)-based differential ion chromatography method that overcomes these limitations. Under optimized conditions (n(H2O2):n(HMS) ≥ 4:1, 60 °C, 30 min), HMS conversion to sulfate reaches 97.5 ± 0.3%, enabling indirect quantification via the stable sulfate signal. Recovery on spiked filters was 99.6 ± 1.4% across 0.025–10 mg L–1, with a method detection limit of 0.018 mg L–1. Application to ∼180 PM2.5 samples from a rural North China Plain site shows HMS is not confined to winter haze: autumn concentrations (mean 0.59 ± 0.70 μg m–3, maximum 3.75 μg m–3) were comparable to or higher than winter values, associated with high relative humidity and elevated formaldehyde. Archived filters lost ∼25% of HMS within one month, suggesting historical data may be biased low. The relative contribution of HMS to particulate sulfur increases as total sulfur loading decreases, implying SO2 emission reductions alone may not diminish HMS chemistry. This method provides a robust framework for accurate HMS measurement and improved sulfur budget closure.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c11813.title: Drivers of Regional Aerosol pH Differences over Eastern China Quantified with a Thermodynamic Framework
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c11813.summary: Abstract Aerosol pH governs atmospheric multiphase chemistry, yet quantifying its regional drivers consistently across meteorologically and chemically diverse regions within a single thermodynamically accurate framework remains challenging. Here, we couple the regional chemical transport model Weather Research and Forecasting-Goddard Earth Observing System with Chemistry (WRF-GC) with the Extended Aerosol Inorganics Model (E-AIM) to compute wintertime aerosol pH over six key target regions of eastern China, decompose the drivers of regional pH differences and intramonthly variability through an ammonia gas-particle partitioning framework, and extend this framework to a scenario-response analysis. Monthly mean pH ranges from 2.54 to 4.32, more acidic in the south and more alkaline at higher latitudes. Temperature is the leading driver of the regional pH deviation in the YRD, PRD, and NEP (contributing 58%–63%), whereas in the high-emission NCP and FWP the deviation is instead dominated by NH3 (41%–58%). Negative covariance among the drivers substantially damps intramonthly pH fluctuations, consistent with multiphase buffering. The sensitivity of pH to ammonia reduction rises sharply as aerosols approach an ammonia-poor regime, such that large emission reductions of ammonia would decrease wintertime aerosol pH well beyond linear expectations, with pronounced inter-regional differences. By resolving these drivers on benchmark-level thermodynamics, these results provide a quantitative, region-specific basis for anticipating how aerosol pH responds to differentiated emission-reduction strategies.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c07283.title: Depth-Dependent eDNA Abundances across Ecosystems Inform Deep-Sea Sampling Strategies
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c07283.summary: Abstract Environmental DNA (eDNA) surveys are increasingly used to assess marine biodiversity and inform deep-sea environmental decision-making, including mineral resource management and fisheries oversight. Yet standard low-volume protocols inherited from coastal work may be inadequate at depth, and recent findings indicate that depth- and productivity-aware sampling, often requiring high-volume in situ filtration, is needed. Currently no quantitative framework links depth and ecosystem context to define defensible filtration volume targets. We compiled 841 eDNA samples from eight expeditions across the North Atlantic, Wider Caribbean Region, and Pacific (surface to 4000 m) to quantify how recoverable eDNA scales with depth and surface productivity, and to derive depth- and productivity-aware sampling targets. Total eDNA concentration declined with depth as a power law, with attenuation exponents (b) modulated by surface productivity: most gradual in eutrophic waters (b = 0.67), intermediate in mesotrophic (b = 0.90), and steepest in oligotrophic systems (b = 1.25). Volume-weighted models explained 66–88% of the variance. At a fixed extract-concentration target, required filtration volumes diverged ∼7-fold between oligotrophic and eutrophic systems at 200 m and ∼38-fold at 4000 m. Conventional Niskin sampling therefore undersamples deep-sea animal eDNA, particularly in mid- to low-productivity systems. Among laboratory parameters, the assay-specific extract-concentration target exerted greater leverage on required volume than extraction efficiency or elution volume. Volume-aware sampling paired with optimized recovery should be routine in deep-sea eDNA surveys.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c12694.title: Shrinking Non-CO2 Emission Inequality in China’s Municipal Wastewater Treatment
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c12694.summary: Abstract Integrating emission equity into climate mitigation is essential for sustainable development but remains poorly understood in the wastewater-treatment sector. Here, we develop a long-term, high-resolution emission inventory covering 8703 municipal wastewater treatment plants across China from 2001 to 2020 to assess methane (CH4) and nitrous oxide (N2O) emission trends and their spatial inequality. National emissions increased substantially, although growth rates slowed after 2010 for CH4 and 2015 for N2O. Discrepancies with IPCC-derived estimates highlight the limitations of population-based approaches in capturing emission trends. Economic development dominated emission growth, with wastewater treatment intensity (wastewater treated per unit of GDP) contributing positively, even under scenarios that account for potential changes in emission factors associated with technological and management improvements. Significant emission inequality persisted, with economically developed cities (9% of the population) contributing 16% and 15% of CH4 and N2O emissions in 2020, whereas the least developed group (45% of the population) accounted for 28% and 32%, respectively. Nonetheless, this disparity narrowed over time with Gini coefficients falling from 0.54 to 0.26 for CH4 and from 0.51 to 0.22 for N2O. These findings support geographically differentiated mitigation strategies that prioritize high-emitting areas to promote effective and equitable climate mitigation.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c15710.title: Source Attribution, Driving Force Interpretation, and Nature-Based Mitigation of Anthropogenic Water Pollution
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c15710.summary: Abstract Anthropogenic pollution induced by combined sewer overflow (CSO) threatens urban aquatic ecosystems, yet the source contributions and driving mechanisms of its pollutants from surface runoff and domestic wastewater remain unclear. Here, we propose an analytical framework coupling high-resolution water quality modeling with climatic and socioeconomic (SSP-RCP) projections to characterize spatiotemporal dynamics and source contributions of CSO pollution under changing environments. Random Forest (RF) with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was employed to identify critical drivers of each source. Lorenz curves and Gini coefficient were introduced to evaluate nature-based solutions (NbS) against extreme CSOs. Application of the framework in a typical urban area demonstrated the dominant contribution of runoff pollution (78–88%) to annual loads of 2500–4200 tons, with uncertainty bounds (UB) of 2300–5800 tons. RF-SHAP analysis revealed nonlinear pollution exacerbation around transition points of approximately 8 days for dry-weather period, 0.45 for surface imperviousness, and 2000 inhabitants/km2 for population density. NbS practices mitigated 19–77% of runoff pollution and 52–76% of domestic pollution, decreasing Gini coefficients from 0.69 to 0.49 (UB: 0.40–0.82). The findings provide quantitative support for compliance with the EU Urban Wastewater Treatment Directive, offering a replicable reference for pollution attribution, driver identification, and mitigation assessment under changing environments.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c07336.title: Meta Life Cycle Assessment, Techno-Economic Analysis, and Risk Assessment of Carbon Mineralization Pathways to Inform Policy Frameworks
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c07336.summary: Abstract Carbon mineralization can reduce both point-source and legacy CO2 emissions while minimizing long-term risk, and it is essential, urgent, and disconnected. There is no holistic governing carbon mineralization policy in the US or EU, even though carbon capture is already factored into all major global climate models, with mineralization (converting CO2 into stable carbonates) representing a major subset. If mineralization is to bolster the suite of climate mitigation strategies, it is vital that academic guidance be provided to inform the currently underinformed policy direction. To address this, this study presents a meta life cycle and techno-economic analysis of carbon mineralization pathways from both academia and industry, normalizing independent techno-economic, life cycle, and risk assessment (Monte Carlo) results within the context of US and EU policy. Results demonstrate that in situ mineralization achieves the greatest life cycle GHG emission reductions at the lowest cost and is the only pathway capable of gigaton-scale emission reductions commensurate with climate goals. Enhanced rock weathering also consistently delivers net-negative GHG removal at relatively low costs, but ex situ pathways achieve lower GHG emission reductions at higher costs, where several proposed pathways are net-CO2 positive as CO2 emitted throughout the process (transportation, electricity use, and natural gas combustion) offsets CO2 sequestered. Risks of leakage, hazards, global capacity, financial impact, and reversal are also quantitatively and qualitatively compared among the mineralization pathways, demonstrating that in situ mineralization has low financial risk when bolstered by state entities, faces uncertainties in non-governmental organization objection, and, ultimately, all pathways are victims of uncharted policy.

doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c11100.title: Field Aging of Biochar Drives SOC Accumulation by Promoting Photosynthetic Carbon Input and Shifting Soil Microbial Communities
doi:10.1021/acs.est.6c11100.summary: Abstract Biochar application is an effective strategy for enhancing the soil organic carbon (SOC) sequestration. However, the extent to which biochar aging affects the SOC sequestration remains unclear. In this study, we investigated SOC dynamics, photosynthetic carbon allocation patterns, and soil microbial characteristics across a 1- to 5-year biochar aging gradient in a wheat farmland. The results revealed that the SOC content increased by 20.7% after 1 year of biochar application, primarily because of an increase in particulate organic carbon (POC), and increased by an additional 14.8% over the next 4 years, which resulted from additional increases in both POC and mineral-associated organic carbon (MAOC). The total 13C assimilation increased by 19.9% and 33.0% after 1 and 5 years of biochar application, respectively. Moreover, biochar application promoted the accumulation of 13C in POC, while 5 years of biochar application also increased the assimilated 13C in MAOC. Furthermore, biochar aging altered the soil bacterial community and increased the abundance of saprotrophic fungi, which were strongly related to SOC dynamics. In summary, our results indicate that biochar aging promotes SOC sequestration by promoting photosynthetic carbon assimilation and facilitating the transformation of plant-derived carbon into SOC related to shifts in the soil microbial community.
